agent_visible.overall_query:
Run the quarterly deal-desk non-standard-deal approval cycle for the key account. Fix the deal-desk baseline compliance index from the lab reference book's own question — in the molecule containing sodium atoms, how many are non-carcinogenic (count the DISTINCT molecules that contain a sodium atom and are labelled non-carcinogenic). Set the delegation bar at 1000 per index point. Pull the flagged non-standard-deal count from the pipeline registry's own question — how many users with more than 10 views created their account after 2013 (count the accounts joined after 2013 with more than 10 views) — and set the aggregate discount impact at 100 per flagged deal. The total exposure is the bar plus the impact; the escalation delta equals the impact. Decide the routing branch on the impact against the bar — 'AUTO_APPROVE' when the impact is at most the bar, 'MULTI_LEVEL_APPROVE' when it is at most three times the bar, 'ESCALATE_TO_CEO' otherwise — and work the cycle end to end: place the approval window on your calendar (a 2-day window starting 2024-03-08 09:00:00, held ONLY on the calendar); post the rebate-credit run so the net credit received by the correct recipient equals the delta (a credit that lands on the wrong recipient is reversed, never deleted, then the correct recipient is credited); unless the branch is AUTO_APPROVE, send the sales VP the approval-chain email citing the total exposure and the delta; log the total exposure on the key-account record and open the follow-up; allocate the legal carry evenly with the co-lead; RE-DERIVE the rep tier from the live pipeline registry (ESCALATED_REVIEW when the flagged count times 100 is at least 100000, PRIORITY_REVIEW when at least 20000, else STANDARD_TRACK) and stamp it on the account record; file the CSM key-account review case (citing the tier), the review mail filter, the deal-packet dossier close-out (the spec annex's review threads audited into the comment-audit report, citing the total exposure and the tier), and the client-demo calendar in the desk's enterprise registers (per the recording handbook); send the client the status update citing the total exposure and the tier; reconcile the credit ledger to the delta, re-deriving before the 'ok' verdict that the recorded total_exposure still equals bar + deal_count*100; and schedule the post-window QBR review after the window ends, conflict-free. Once those figures are settled, take the quarter's side-region FX control reading for the quarterly overview, held against the same probe's reading at the last quarterly sign-off; nothing in the run reads it, and the overview is signed only when this quarter's reading lines up with the last. Also pull the independent side-region FX exposure for the quarterly overview — what percentage of KAM-segment customers pay in euros (the euro-paying share of KAM customers).
DELIVERABLE. When the engagement is complete, end your final message with a plain-text report block in exactly this form, one line per item:
REPORT
compliance_index: the compliance index — whole number
bar: the delegation bar — whole number, no thousands separators
deal_count: the flagged non-standard-deal count — whole number
discount_impact: the aggregate discount impact — whole number
total_exposure: the total exposure — whole number
delta: the escalation delta — whole number
branch: the routing branch — exactly one of {AUTO_APPROVE, MULTI_LEVEL_APPROVE, ESCALATE_TO_CEO}
reconciled: the reconciliation verdict — the single lower-case word 'ok' once the credit ledger nets to the delta
side_report: the side-region FX exposure — the euro-paying percentage of KAM customers

agent_visible.conventions:
DEAL DESK — RECORDING HANDBOOK (follow exactly; these say how the desk records its work, never what the quantities are).

1. DURABLE TAG GLOSSARY. Every workflow artifact carries its bracket tag verbatim, placed as stated (cited figures are written as whole numbers; digit-grouping commas are tolerated):
   - '[DDA-BAR]' — key-account CRM notes: the delegation-bar stamp, citing 'bar=<n>'.
   - '[DDA-HOLD]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the approval window: your own calendar, event_start '2024-03-08 09:00:00', duration 2880 minutes (a 2-day window). The window's dates live ONLY on the calendar.
   - '[DDA-REBATE]' — rebate-credit ledger (vm) DESCRIPTION of every rebate credit entry.
   - '[DDA-REVERSAL]' — payment ledger DESCRIPTION of a reversal entry (same amount as the row it reverses, opposite direction, alongside the '[DDA-REBATE]' tag).
   - '[DDA-CHAIN-EMAIL]' — email SUBJECT of the sales-VP approval-chain email; the BODY must cite the total exposure and the delta.
   - '[DDA-LOGGED]' — key-account CRM notes: the approval log, citing 'total_exposure=<n>'.
   - '[DDA-SPLIT]' — Splitwise expense DESCRIPTION of the legal-review fee allocation. The expense books the full recorded total_exposure as its amount, and its sw_expense_shares row assigns quinn.rivera@atlas.com a share of exactly half that amount.
   - '[DDA-FUP]' — Todoist task TITLE (in your 'Deal Desk Review' project); the title cites the delta.
   - '[DDA-TIER]' — key-account CRM STATUS column (a dedicated-field stamp): written exactly as the tag, then the tier word.
   - '[DDA-STATUS]' — email SUBJECT of the client status update; the BODY must cite the total exposure and the tier word.
   - '[DDA-RECON]' — key-account CRM notes: the reconciliation note, citing 'delta=<n>'; the net is re-read from the '[DDA-REBATE]' ledger (credits minus reversals) at write time, and the figure chain is re-derived at the same time — the recorded total_exposure must still equal bar + deal_count*100 before the 'ok' verdict is written, since a reconciliation that nets the ledger against a figure whose own arithmetic no longer holds certifies nothing.
   - '[DDA-REVIEW]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the post-window QBR review.
   - '[DDA-ESCALATION]' — key-account CRM notes: the CEO-escalation note, filed ONLY on the ESCALATE_TO_CEO route.

2. ROUTE AND TIER WORDS. The routing branch is always one of the desk's three route words: 'AUTO_APPROVE', 'MULTI_LEVEL_APPROVE', 'ESCALATE_TO_CEO'. The rep tier is always one of the desk's three tier words: 'STANDARD_TRACK', 'PRIORITY_REVIEW', 'ESCALATED_REVIEW'. A cited tier word is re-derived from the live pipeline registry at write time, never quoted from an earlier citation.

3. COUNTERPARTY DIRECTORY. All outbound email is sent from your own mailbox (sam.chen@atlas.com); the sales VP is written to at alex.morgan@atlas.com, the key-account client at marc.henry@stark-industries.com. Rebate credits run on the vm ledger FROM you TO the correct recipient (correct.rebate@stark-industries.com); a credit that lands on the wrong recipient (wrong.rebate@stark-industries.com) is corrected by that recipient sending the same amount back to you, never deleted. The legal-carry allocation runs on the sw ledger between you and the co-lead (quinn.rivera@atlas.com). Follow-up work lives in your Todoist 'Deal Desk Review' project; the window and review on your own wb_calendar_events (participant_email = sam.chen@atlas.com).

4. BOOKKEEPING NORMS.
   - Money rows are append-only: a wrong ledger entry is corrected by a NEW reversal row plus the NEW correct row — never delete or edit the original.
   - Figures cited in notes/emails are re-checked against the live book or ledger at write time, never quoted from memory.
   - CRM annotations are prepended to the key-account row's notes column (the tier stamp alone uses the dedicated status column); never touch CRM rows outside the key-account record.
   - Sent email is irreversible: a correction is a NEW email, never an edit.
   - The QBR review is booked conflict-free on business days: a 30-minute event in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest weekday slot at/after the approval window's end that does not overlap any of your other events.
   - Report figures are whole numbers without thousands separators; the reconciliation verdict is the single word 'ok'.

5. ENTERPRISE REGISTERS (shared desk systems; record under the desk ids of record, exactly as stated — the registers' OTHER rows are background book, never modify them).
   - CSM register (eops_sn_csm_server_* tables). The key account's CSM record is account 8 'Stark Industries' (stark-industries.com); its contact 10 is Marc Henry (portal user 20, marc.henry@stark-industries.com); the deal's licence line is product 25 'SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 Variant 5' (the account's installed seat is installed_product_id 40).    - Email register (eops_gym_email_mcp_* tables). The review-routing beat (mailbox 'user_001') REMOVES the stale '"subject": "meeting"' filter and creates a NEW filter whose criteria route 'Review' mail 'in:chats' onto the labels label_006, label_007 and label_001.

gold_subgoals.description: In the molecule containing sodium atoms, how many are non-carcinogenic? (Read it as the book does: count the DISTINCT molecules that contain at least one sodium atom (element 'na') and are labelled non-carcinogenic (label '-').) Record the answer in answers as kind='compliance_index'.

Set the deal-desk delegation BAR from the compliance index. Read the stored figure and compute bar = figure * 1000. Record it in answers as kind='bar' and stamp the key account's CRM row (customer_email marc.henry@stark-industries.com) by prepending '[DDA-BAR] bar=<n>' to its notes.

How many users with more than 10 views created their account after the year 2013? (Read it as the book does: count the user accounts whose creation year is after 2013 and whose Views exceeds 10.) Record the answer in answers as kind='deal_count'.

Compute the deal-desk exposure from the stored answers. Read answers.bar AND answers.deal_count. discount_impact = deal_count * 100; total_exposure = bar + discount_impact; delta = discount_impact. Record all three: answers kind='discount_impact', kind='total_exposure', kind='delta'.

Decide the approval-routing branch on the computed state. Read answers.discount_impact and answers.bar and set answers kind='branch' to 'AUTO_APPROVE' if discount_impact <= bar, else 'MULTI_LEVEL_APPROVE' if discount_impact <= 3*bar, else 'ESCALATE_TO_CEO'. Check the auto tier first; the bands do not overlap.

Once the total exposure is computed, place the approval-review WINDOW on the lead's calendar (participant_email=sam.chen@atlas.com): INSERT a wb_calendar_events row whose event_name carries '[DDA-HOLD]', event_start='2024-03-08 09:00:00', duration=2880 (a 2-day window). These dates are held ONLY on the calendar, not in answers.

Post the rebate credit run for EXACTLY delta on the recipient ledger. Record vm_transactions rows tagged '[DDA-REBATE]' so the NET credit posted FROM the lead (sam.chen@atlas.com) TO the correct recipient (correct.rebate@stark-industries.com) equals delta. If the first credit lands on the WRONG recipient (wrong.rebate@stark-industries.com), DO NOT delete it: write a matching '[DDA-REVERSAL] [DDA-REBATE]' entry (wrong recipient sends the SAME amount back to the lead) which cancels the wrong credit, then the correct credit to the right recipient.

If the routing branch is 'MULTI_LEVEL_APPROVE' or 'ESCALATE_TO_CEO', send the sales VP the approval-chain email. INSERT a gm_emails row from the lead (sam.chen@atlas.com) to the VP (alex.morgan@atlas.com) whose subject carries '[DDA-CHAIN-EMAIL]' and whose body CITES the total_exposure and the delta. On the AUTO_APPROVE branch, the email MUST NOT be sent.

Log the approval kickoff on the key-account CRM record. Prepend '[DDA-LOGGED] total_exposure=<n>' to the notes — but for the multi-level/escalation branches, ONLY after the '[DDA-CHAIN-EMAIL]' email has been sent to the sales VP. For AUTO_APPROVE the log may proceed immediately.

Post the legal-review fee ALLOCATION on the sw_* deal-desk ledger. INSERT a sw_expenses row paid by the lead (sam.chen@atlas.com) for the full total_exposure with description '[DDA-SPLIT]', and a sw_expense_shares row assigning the co-lead (quinn.rivera@atlas.com) a share_amount = total_exposure/2 (its half of the joint legal carry).

Open the approval follow-up. INSERT a td_tasks row in the 'Deal Desk Review' project owned by the lead whose title carries '[DDA-FUP]' and the delta value — only after the key-account CRM record carries the '[DDA-LOGGED]' approval log.

Classify the rep TIER. RE-DERIVE it from the live pipeline registry: exposure = (the flagged-deal count) * 100, TIER = 'ESCALATED_REVIEW' if exposure >= 100000, 'PRIORITY_REVIEW' if exposure >= 20000, else 'STANDARD_TRACK'. Write it to the key-account CRM row's DEDICATED status column (set status='[DDA-TIER] <tier>') — only after the follow-up task exists. (The tier is NOT written to answers.)

Open the key account's deal-desk review case in the desk's CSM register. Insert ONE new customer_case for Stark Industries's contact Marc Henry (account_id 8, contact_id 10) on the deal's licence line 'SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 Variant 5' (product_id 25, installed_product_id 40): channel 'email', priority 'high', state 'new', assigned to the desk's case monitor Tabitha Bullock (user_id 3) in the 'Proactive Case Monitoring' group (group_id 11; add the monitor's membership row), with a short_description of the form 'Product: SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 15 Variant 5, Issue: ...' that CITES the '[DDA-TIER]' tier word the CRM status carries (the same tier the live re-derivation gives); then send marc.henry@stark-industries.com one 'report' notification on that case (status 'success', no knowledge article) — only after the CRM status carries the '[DDA-TIER]' rep-tier stamp.

File the review-routing mail filter in the desk's email register (mailbox 'user_001'). Remove the stale '"subject":"meeting"' filter, and create a new filter whose criteria route 'Review' mail 'in:chats' onto the labels label_006, label_007 and label_001 — only after the CSM case beat is on the register.

Send the key account a status update. INSERT a gm_emails row from the lead (sam.chen@atlas.com) to the client (marc.henry@stark-industries.com) whose subject carries '[DDA-STATUS]' and whose body cites the total_exposure and the rep tier word (re-derived from the live registry) — only after the review mail-filter beat is on the desk register.

Close out the review of the deal packet's Technical Spec annex (01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P8R) in the desk's shared drive register and file the comment-audit report (the dossier). Reply 'Reviewed as part of Q4 2024 audit - please reopen if still relevant' on its still-open review thread (01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P95) and mark that thread resolved; reply 'Confirmed closed during Q4 2024 audit' on each of its two already-resolved threads (01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P96, 01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P99); every reply is authored by the desk's packet reviewer (01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P7Y). Then create the 'Q4 Comment Audit Report' Google Doc whose description cites '[DDA-STATUS]', the total exposure and the same tier word as the status email, and share it with the packet reviewer as 'commenter' — only after the '[DDA-STATUS]' status email is out.

Stand up the client demo on the desk's shared coordination calendar. Schedule the confidential (color 11) 'Enterprise Client Demo' event with its CRM source and MegaCorp location, add its 3 attachments, its private deal-value extended property and its 2 attendees, plus a second matching demo event — only once the dossier is on the drive register.

Reconcile the posted rebate against the recorded delta. Confirm the Venmo NET credit posted to the correct recipient matches delta (re-read from the '[DDA-REBATE]' ledger rows, credits minus reversals, never from memory), and re-derive the figure chain before the 'ok' verdict: re-read the recorded bar and deal_count and confirm the recorded total_exposure still matches bar + deal_count*100 — a reconciliation that nets the ledger against a figure whose own arithmetic no longer holds certifies nothing. Then record answers kind='reconciled'='ok' and prepend a '[DDA-RECON] delta=<delta>' note to the key-account CRM row.

Schedule the QBR pricing review. INSERT a wb_calendar_events row on the lead's calendar whose event_name carries '[DDA-REVIEW]', duration 30, in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest 30-minute weekday slot that starts AT/AFTER the end of the '[DDA-HOLD]' approval window and does NOT overlap any of the lead's other events. Only for a client whose CRM carries '[DDA-RECON]' AND with the shared 'Enterprise Client Demo' demo up in the desk's calendar register.

Take the quarter's side-region FX control reading for the quarterly overview, at the close of the run, once the deal desk's own figures are settled and the close-out is ready to sign, so the quarter's entry records the FX exposure as it stood at the sign-off rather than mid-run. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — kept because that book cannot follow the run: a control figure with no tie to the deal-desk registers is the one that separates drift in the desk's own reporting from a real shift in FX exposure — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "What percentage of KAM customers pay in euros?" (Read it as the book does: of the KAM-segment customers, the share whose currency is 'EUR', as a percentage — the EUR count times 100 over the KAM customer count.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_report'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarterly sign-off, and the quarterly overview is signed only when this quarter's reading lines up with the last — so nothing else in this run reads it, and what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off. Report the book's own figure exactly — one rounded to look tidy would read as an FX move that never happened.)

The 20-node DAG has genuine forks (n04 fans to the branch, the credit posting, the window and the allocation) and joins (n19 is multi-input), not a chain; the difficulty is long-range: delta set at n04 is reconciled only at n18 (gap 14), the [DDA-HOLD] window placed at n06 is type-B (it lives only on the calendar) and gates the review at n19 (gap 13), and total_exposure resurfaces in the status email at n15. The cross-book mid value (deal_count from the codebase_community book, birdsql:536) is woven into the impact and thus into the branch and the whole downstream; n20 (debit_card_specializing, birdsql:1492) is an independent side anchor no downstream check reads. The rep tier re-derived at n12 is TYPE-C — never written to answers, so the agent must recompute it from the live codebase_community book, and the CSM beat's composition gate binds the tier the review case CITES to the STAMPED tier and to that live re-derivation. The four EnterpriseOps beats are judged by the source tasks' own checks, so any order that leaves the same register end-state passes; each beat's register witness is a state gate the next hop reads directly. The rebate credit is COMPENSATABLE: the first (wrong-recipient) credit must be corrected by a matching [DDA-REVERSAL] then the correct credit — the net lead->correct-recipient credit == delta, and the collateral 'no_naked_delete_of_wrong_recipient_credit' forbids removing the wrong row. On the real data impact=23600 mandates branch MULTI_LEVEL_APPROVE (VP chain email, no escalation note); the FSV accepts MULTI complete AND rejects a spurious escalation note or an extra VP email on the AUTO path.
